newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $61.50, passed-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $61.50, passed-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle early Thursday were bid $61.50 per cwt and passed by owners asking $62.00 to $63.00, feedlot sources said.
Packer bids were steady with the top of Wednesday's range in light trading at $61.00-$61.50.
"I think we'll see more cattle trade today, and I think it could be better," one Kansas feedlot operator said.
Kansas feedlots still had cattle to sell, but Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma feedlots reportedly had sold most of their showlists, cattle feeders in those areas said.
That leaves the door open for firm prices, some said.

Most of this week's sales occured Monday at $62 and there were reports that packers were already starting to pick up cattle at several feedlots in Kansas and the Texas Panhandle, suggesting needs were greater than expected, sources said.

Weak beef prices this week curbed packer bids and weighed on fed cattle prices, but a surge in beef sales on Wednesday had some sources optimistic the strong demand would spur increased packer buying and put a floor under cattle prices.
Boxed beef cut-out prices on Wednesday were quoted down $0.45 to $1.07 per cwt, but USDA reported 338 fabricated beef loads sold.
